subject: Re: Vendor onboarding / PO & commit structure for Hosted API
messages:
From: Susan Huang <susan.huang@acme.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Vendor onboarding docs & PO terms

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is impressed with the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to surface two items before we can issue an initial PO: 1) our preferred vendor form (attached), and 2) confirmation of billing terms (Net30) and whether you can accept our standard tax & invoice language.

Separately, our finance lead pushed back on pure per-token usage pricing for Hosted API. They prefer a predictable monthly commit with a usage true-up. Can you confirm whether Redwood offers committed tiers (monthly or annual) that guarantee a per-token discount, and how true-ups are calculated? We want to avoid large month-to-month variability.

I've attached Acme_Purchase_Terms.pdf for your legal team. Please let us know if you can complete the vendor form or if an addendum is required.

Thanks,
Susan Huang
Procurement Manager, Acme AI
Attach: Acme_Purchase_Terms.pdf (PDF, 182 KB)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Susan Huang <susan.huang@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding docs & PO terms

Hi Susan — appreciate the clear ask and the file. Quick answers up front: we can accept Net30 invoicing and we have committed tiers that provide per-token discounts; we typically structure them as monthly or annual spend commitments with a per-token true-up at the end of each billing period.

I've attached our latest pricing summary (redwood_pricing_summary_v2.pdf) which shows the commit tiers we commonly use and the discount schedule. High-level options we can do today:
- Month-to-month usage with volume discounts applied at invoice (no commit)
- Monthly minimum commit with usage-based true-up (preferred by many customers)
- Annual committed spend (best unit economics; contract required)

If Acme wants the vendor form completed, we'll need your procurement team to confirm which contract governs (your PO with our standard terms vs. a signed addendum). Marissa (cc'd) can scope a short addendum that maps your vendor form fields to Redwood's standard terms — that avoids re-negotiating the full MSA.

Next step: can you confirm the approximate target monthly spend range so we can propose a specific commit tier? Also looping in Priyom from sales ops for invoice flow/questions.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Attach: redwood_pricing_summary_v2.pdf (PDF, 95 KB)
From: Susan Huang <susan.huang@acme.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@acme.ai>, procurement@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:27:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding docs & PO terms

Thanks Sean.

Acme is planning a ramp: pilot month ~$15k, production months expected to be $40k–$60k depending on adoption. Finance wants a floor to cap our monthly exposure and predictability — ideally a monthly minimum commit and a per-month true-up, not pure usage invoicing.

Procurement also prefers that vendors complete our preferred vendor form rather than drafting an addendum; they say it speeds PO issuance. We can be flexible on minor wording but they generally won't accept major deviations from the form fields.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood is able to accept a PO referencing an SOW and invoice monthly for actual usage with a true-up? If so, our legal will route the PO and we can sign once the vendor form is complete.

Let me know what you need from our side to keep this moving.

Best,
Susan
Attach: (no new attachments)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Vendor onboarding docs & PO terms — Acme AI (procurement pushback)

Team — forwarding Acme's procurement note. Key asks: they want the vendor form filled and a monthly minimum commit with true-up. Pilot/production spend band attached above.

Options I see (pros/cons):
1) Accept preferred vendor form as-is and sign PO referencing our MSA. Legal risk: some fields conflict with our indemnity/limit-of-liability/warranty language — would need minimal exceptions.
2) Execute a short addendum (RWI_PO_Addendum.docx) mapping their vendor form answers to Redwood terms; cleaner from our side but procurement may push back on added steps.
3) Offer a hybrid pricing structure: monthly minimum commit (e.g., $10k/mo) for first 3 months, with usage true-up and tiered per-token discounts applied retroactively each month when thresholds are hit. This reduces their variability while preserving usage economics.

Proposed commercial: pilot month = $10k minimum, months 2–12: $10k monthly minimum; if monthly usage exceeds $50k equivalent, apply 7% discount on token unit price for that month; if annualized commit hits $300k, apply 10% contract-level discount. We can document calculation in the addendum and agree to Net30 invoicing.

Can legal (Laura) advise on whether we can accept the vendor form answers or if we should push for addendum? Marissa — once we have legal sign-off I can offer the hybrid commercial to Susan and seek a PO.

Thanks,
Sean

Sean / Marissa — thanks for the proposal and looping legal. Procurement reviewed the addendum draft and is willing to accept a short mapping addendum rather than reworking our entire vendor form. They also accepted the monthly minimum approach as long as the minimum is aligned with our forecast.

Acme will issue an initial PO referencing your MSA + RWI_PO_Addendum.docx with a $10,000 monthly minimum for months 1–3 and a true-up at month-end. If monthly usage exceeds $50k, we'll accept the 7% discount for that month. Net30 acceptable. Please send a DocuSign for the addendum so we can route internally.

Next steps we expect from Redwood: 1) finalize the short addendum and send via DocuSign, 2) Redwood confirms the invoice line items and PO number placement, and 3) we receive a signed copy of the addendum to attach to our PO.

If that all looks good, we'll issue the PO tomorrow.

Best,
